summary: The narrator, Cas Russell, has just left custody and phones Checker, a forger who says he produced the paperwork that freed her. Checker brags about the speed of the job, waives his fee because he owes her for saving Arthur and is grateful she kept Arthur alive, and sounds pleased to be thanked. When Cas complains that Arthur gets hung up on small rules despite breaking many laws, Checker defends him sharply, and the call ends with his tone unreadable. The passage also shows Cas's unease with owing favors and with a internalized copy of Tresting who keeps judging her conscience.
one_line: A freed narrator phones forger Checker, who waives his fee and defends Arthur after a tense exchange about loyalty and debts.
key_facts: The narrator leaves the station at night, when an almost-full moon hangs above the city and traffic has thinned.
Checker texts or is contacted via the message "U OUT?" and the narrator dials back.
Checker says he had to forge a large amount of paperwork to free the narrator and calls the job "record-breaking."
Checker says the narrator's fingerprints are "disappearing as we speak" from records.
Checker says having nothing in the system gave him a window to work with.
The narrator says being freed feels good because she no longer has to be trapped in the station.
Checker says he will not charge for the job because he owed the narrator for saving Arthur, and he is grateful she kept Arthur alive.
The narrator dislikes owing people favors and is uneasy about accepting the free work.
Checker asks the narrator not to tell Arthur about the favor, since Arthur does not like it when Checker does things like this.
The narrator says Arthur has broken more laws than she can count yet gets hung up on small matters, and calls him inconsistent.
Checker responds sharply that Arthur is "good people" and tells the narrator not to insult him.
The narrator says a copy of Tresting has taken up residence in her head and keeps track of her conscience.
Checker tells Cas Russell that she may impress him with her knowledge of Bayesian probability but should not insult Arthur.
The call ends with Checker silent and the narrator unable to read his tone.
